paper_title: Parallel (1+e)-Approximate Multi-Commodity Min-Cost Flow in Almost Optimal Depth and Work
authors: Bernhard Haeupler (University of Sofia "St. Kliment Ohridski" and ETH Zürich), Yonggang Jiang (MPI-INF and Saarland University), Yaowei Long (University of Michigan), Thatchaphol Saranurak (University of Michigan), Shengzhe Wang (ETH Zürich)
statement: Open Problem 1. Are there parallel (1 + ϵ)-approximate algorithms for either (edge-capacitated) min-cost flows or vertex-capacitated maximum flows, with nearly-linear work and polylogarithmic depth?
context: Polylogarithmic Depth. A natural and important open problem is to further reduce the depth from subpolynomial to polylogarithmic while retaining almost-optimal work or improving toward nearly-optimal work, even in the single-commodity setting. As we discussed in Section I, (1+ϵ)-approximate parallel algorithms with polylogarithmic depth and nearly-linear work are known for shortest paths [1]–[3] and (edge-capacitated) maxflows [5]. However, it remains unclear whether similar results (particularly polylogarithmic depth) can be achieved for the (edge-capacitated) min-cost flow problem or vertexcapacitated maxflow problem. Open Problem 1. Are there parallel (1 + ϵ)-approximate algorithms for either (edge-capacitated) min-cost flows or vertex-capacitated maximum flows, with nearly-linear work and polylogarithmic depth? Open Problem 2. Is there distributed (1 + ϵ)-approximate min-cost flow algorithm with almost-optimal round complexity in the CONGEST model? We note that our approach may potentially transfer to the distributed setting, since the main building blocks, including length-constrained expander decompositions, sparse neighborhood cover, and approximate length-constrained maxflows, all admit efficient distributed algorithms. Recall that LCflow shortcuts have the following quality measures: length slack, congestion slack, step, and size.
